title: Search in a Binary Search Tree
description: Given the root of a binary search tree and a target value, determine whether the target exists in the tree.
inputFormat: Second line: n values inserted into the BST
outputFormat: Print true if target exists; otherwise print false.

title: Insert into a Binary Search Tree
description: Insert a value into a BST containing unique values and print its inorder traversal.
inputFormat: Second line: n values inserted into the BST
outputFormat: Print the inorder traversal after insertion.
constraints: The new value is not already present

examples.explanation: Inorder traversal of a BST is sorted.

title: Minimum Value in a BST
description: Find the minimum value stored in a non-empty binary search tree.
inputFormat: Second line: n values inserted into the BST

examples.explanation: The leftmost node contains the minimum.

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
description: Given a binary tree in level order, determine whether every node satisfies the strict BST ordering rules.
inputFormat: Second line: n level-order tokens; use null for missing nodes
outputFormat: Print true if valid; otherwise print false.
constraints: Node values fit in signed 32-bit integers

examples.explanation: Both children satisfy the BST ordering.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of BST
description: Given a BST and two existing values p and q, find the value of their lowest common ancestor.
inputFormat: Second line: n values inserted into the BST
outputFormat: Print the lowest common ancestor value.

examples.explanation: 2 and 8 lie on opposite sides of 6.

title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
description: Return the kth smallest value in a BST with unique values.
inputFormat: Second line: n values inserted into the BST

title: Delete a Node from a BST
description: Delete the node with the given key from a BST and print the inorder traversal of the resulting tree.
inputFormat: Second line: n values inserted into the BST
outputFormat: Print the inorder traversal after deletion.

title: Binary Search Tree Iterator
description: Print all BST values in ascending order using an iterator that uses O(h) extra memory.
inputFormat: Second line: n values inserted into the BST
outputFormat: Print values returned by successive iterator calls.

title: Recover Binary Search Tree
description: Exactly two values in a BST were swapped. Restore the BST and print its inorder traversal.
inputFormat: Second line: n level-order tokens representing the corrupted BST
outputFormat: Print the inorder traversal after recovery.
constraints: Exactly two node values are swapped

title: Largest BST Subtree
description: Given a binary tree, find the number of nodes in its largest subtree that is also a valid BST.
inputFormat: Second line: n level-order tokens; use null for missing nodes
outputFormat: Print the size of the largest BST subtree.

examples.explanation: The subtree rooted at 5 is a BST of size 3.
